text:
taylor: hi everyone, first day snag. accepted the org invite but cloning private repos gives 403 and web shows 'You must enable 2FA' even though I turned on 2FA last night. accepted the invite with taylor.personal@gmail.com then re-accepted with taylor@redwood.com. any ideas?
it-help: welcome! do `ssh -T git@github.com` and paste the output. also double-check which email is primary on your GitHub profile.
taylor: `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi taylorold! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.` so SSH is authenticating to my old personal account.
frank: that explains it. your SSH key is tied to the wrong GH account or your ssh-agent is offering the old key. run `ssh-add -l` to list keys and `ssh-add -D` to clear then add the correct key.
taylor: `ssh-add -l` shows two keys. i did `ssh-add -D` then `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood`. now `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi taylored! You've successfully authenticated...`
onboard-bot: SCIM: user taylor@redwood.com provisioned -> teams: platform, api.
taylor: ok now it auths to the right account but cloning still fails with HTTP 403 in the browser and git clone says "Repository not found."
lucy: did you authorize the org SSO? go to Profile -> Organizations -> Redwood Inference and click "Authorize" if prompted. SSO blocks access to org repos until you authorize.
taylor: i clicked authorize and re-authenticated with Okta. also switched to SSH remote: `git@github.com:redwood/inference-examples.git` but still got "Repository not found."
frank: double-check the SSH key isn't also registered as a deploy key on a different repo. deploy keys are repo-scoped and can prevent the key from being used as a user key. run `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood.pub` and i'll check.
taylor: fingerprint is `SHA256:examplefingerprintabc123`.
frank: that fingerprint is currently attached as a deploy key on docs.redwood. i've filed a ticket to remove it and re-add as a user key; in the meantime add a new key to your GitHub account and use that.
taylor: added a new key, re-tested and `ssh -T` -> `Hi taylornw! You've successfully authenticated`. clone succeeded, pushed a tiny README. :tada: thanks all.
it-help: noted: onboarding doc update request to 1) send invites to work emails only, 2) remind hires to authorize SSO before creating PATs, 3) include ssh-agent troubleshooting snippet. welcome aboard @taylor :wave:
